variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'when he heard those words' renders a temporal infinitive construct; both the qere kaph (כְּשָׁמְעוֹ, 'as/when he heard') and the ketiv beth (בשמעו, 'in his hearing' = 'when he heard') yield the same English 'when he heard'. No italics or textual note; the base qere fallback carries the projection.

review_notes: Corrected be-yad ha-mmal'akhim → by the hand of messengers: the rectum carries an article and the ASV renders messengers anarthrous with the single the before the construct, so under rule 29 that the is fronted and belongs to the article (s016), while yad takes only hand. The accepted alignment had supplied the the on the construct and left the present article unrepresented, against rule 29's direction to supply a the on a construct only where no article morpheme is present.
ASV margin (a terror from Jehovah) read and set aside; printed text governs.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'by the time the sun is hot' renders a temporal infinitive construct; the qere kaph (כְּחֹם, 'as the sun is hot') and the ketiv beth (בחם, 'in the heat of') are both compatible with this English, and 'by the time' does not favour either preposition.
